legend: Ridham's birthday is coming up and he really loves primes and permutations. Knowing this Aastik decided to gift Ridham a permutation a%%ZSMJ0%% of length n%%ZSMJ1%% such that ai+an−i+1%%ZSMJ2%% is prime for all i%%ZSMJ3%% such that 1≤i≤n%%ZSMJ4%%, but just when Aastik sat down to generate this permutation he realised that he did not know how to make such a permutation. Help Aastik to prepare the gift for Ridham.

A permutation of length n%%ZSMJ5%% is an array consisting of n%%ZSMJ6%% distinct integers from 1%%ZSMJ7%% to n%%ZSMJ8%% in arbitrary order. For example, [2,3,1,5,4]%%ZSMJ9%% is a permutation, but [1,2,2]%%ZSMJ10%% is not a permutation (2%%ZSMJ11%% appears twice in the array), and [1,3,4]%%ZSMJ12%% is also not a permutation (n=3%%ZSMJ13%% but there is 4%%ZSMJ14%% in the array).
input: The first line contains a single integer t%%ZSMJ15%% (1≤t≤104%%ZSMJ16%%). The description of the test cases follows.
The first line and only line of each test case contains an integer n%%ZSMJ17%% (1≤n≤106%%ZSMJ18%%) — the size of the permutation a%%ZSMJ19%%.
The sum of n%%ZSMJ20%% over all testcases does not exceed 3⋅106%%ZSMJ21%%.
output: For each testcase, output n%%ZSMJ22%% integers — the elements of the required permutation. If it's not possible, output −1%%ZSMJ23%%.
